summary: Kickoff for a POC to validate harness integration and benchmark acceptance criteria. Focus: customer script compatibility, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, SLA targets (p50/p95/p99), KV cache warmup, and telemetry contract. Agreed to an initial smoke run followed by a throughput sweep; timeline ~2-4 weeks for measurable results. Security and adapter deliverables pinned as pre-reqs.
topics: workload sizing (rps, concurrency, tokens per request)
streaming vs non-streaming client adapter behavior
KV cache warmup and prefix caching
acceptance criteria and SLA targets (latency and error budget)
transcript_header:
Date: 2026-04-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jesse Harper (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Lumina Eng Manager), Tomás Rueda (Lumina SRE), Leah Goldman (Lumina Product), Samir Ahmed (Lumina ML), Zoe Li (Lumina Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Jesse Harper: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm jesse, AE on the account. aim for a ~1hr kickoff to align on harness integration and acceptance.
[00:12] Priya Patel: thanks, jesse. quick context, Lumina has a triage assistant we want to put behind an inference layer. main constraints: strict p99 tail for clinical suggestions and on-prem data residency for PHI.
[00:28] Maya Chen: great context. i want to understand the scripts you run today — are they streaming (token-by-token) or batch call per request? that will change the harness adapter.
[00:42] Tomás Rueda: most traffic is single-request per patient note, but there are two modes: interactive clinician flow (streaming desirable) and nightly bulk scoring (non-streaming).
[00:56] Leah Goldman: yes, interactive is top priority, we need sub-500ms p95 for short prompts, longer prompts can be okay at p95 ~1s but p99 needs to be stable.
[01:12] Devon Park: ok noted. can you give us expected tokens per request distribution? even rough percentiles helps.
[01:20] Samir Ahmed: sure, median ~120 tokens, 95th ~850 tokens, rare long tails to 3k. attached we'll send the histogram.
[01:35] Jesse Harper: perfect. so for the POC we propose a two-stage run: 1) smoke harness — adapter + small throughput test to validate end-to-end script compatibility and streaming handshake, 2) throughput sweep to find concurrency and batching sweet spot and measure p50/p95/p99 under representative load.
[01:57] Priya Patel: timeline? we have compliance windows and can't run long tests during our change freeze next week.
[02:05] Maya Chen: understood — smoke can be this week if you provide scripts, throughput sweep early next week. total bench work about 2-3 days plus analysis.
[02:16] Zoe Li: on security, what data touches Redwood? because PHI rules, we need encryption in transit + at rest and keys under our KMS or HSM ideally.
[02:28] Jesse Harper: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS as well. we'll share SOC2 and our audit log schema.
[02:43] Tomás Rueda: do you keep full transcripts in logs? we need redact or not retain raw patient data.
[02:52] Maya Chen: telemetry contract we propose collects request id, model id, token counts, latency buckets, and anonymized error codes; we do not store full prompt text unless customer opts in.
[03:05] Priya Patel: that's acceptable but need explicit docs.
[03:09] Jesse Harper: we'll send the security appendix.
[03:12] Leah Goldman: back to harness — what's the adapter surface? language/runtime? we run Python 3.10 microservices and some GO workers.
[03:22] Devon Park: our harness provides example adapters in Python and Go. typical work: plug in a client adapter shim, confirm streaming callback semantics (on_token/on_done), and validate backpressure.
[03:35] Samir Ahmed: specifics — do you maintain a KV cache across requests for prefix caching? that affects warmup and latency numbers.
[03:44] Maya Chen: yes, runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. for the POC we should test cold-start vs warmed cache — we'll do a warmup phase to simulate persistent sessions and also cold restarts to measure tail.
[03:58] Tomás Rueda: how are batching semantics handled for streaming? we worry that batching may delay first token.
[04:06] Devon Park: good point — we have configurable batching windows and can set a max-latency threshold so streaming first-token latency stays low; the tradeoff is throughput efficiency. we'll include both streaming-first-token and end-to-end latency metrics.
[04:22] Jesse Harper: acceptance criteria proposal: p95 streaming-first-token < 300ms for interactive flow, p95 end-to-end < 500ms for median prompts, p99 end-to-end < 1.2s for 95th percentile token lengths, and error rate <0.5% under target load. any objections?
[04:45] Leah Goldman: p95s look aggressive but doable if quantization is conservative; for p99 maybe we want a little more buffer — can we add a clause for fallback behavior if breached?
[04:55] Maya Chen: yes, fallback to a slightly higher-capacity instance or to non-quantized model when p99 breaches — that's part of graceful degradation. we'll document rollout/fallback policy.
[05:08] Priya Patel: also want to define cost visibility — token-level cost breakdown per route for the POC so we can compare hosted vs dedicated.
[05:18] Jesse Harper: we'll produce a cost estimate sheet for the run and expected per-1M token delta for quantized vs fp16 models.
[05:27] Tomás Rueda: telemetry — we need raw traces for first run to diagnose outliers, but after that we prefer aggregated metrics.
[05:36] Maya Chen: agreed. initial run will include verbose traces (sanitized) and then aggregate telemetry thereafter.
[05:44] Priya Patel: what's the expected engineering effort on our side?
[05:48] Devon Park: mostly wiring the adapter to call the harness and provide scripts as input. we estimate 1-2 engineer days to integrate the adapter and a half day for smoke verification.
[05:58] Samir Ahmed: ok that's reasonable.
[06:02] Jesse Harper: RACI recap and timeline: Jesse to share harness README + python adapter by 4/30; Lumina to give scripts + histograms by 5/4; we run smoke 5/5-5/6 and do throughput sweep 5/7-5/8; follow-up on 5/11 to review results — is that aligned?
[06:19] Priya Patel: yes aligned pending security docs.
[06:23] Zoe Li: i'll review the security appendix and confirm KMS approach.
[06:26] Leah Goldman: one more thing — can we capture functional acceptance tests? e.g., hallucination rate threshold on a labeled sample set.
[06:35] Maya Chen: absolutely — include evaluation set and automatic quality regression check as part of acceptance. we'll need example prompts and expected outputs from Lumina.
[06:45] Jesse Harper: great; i'll add quality check to the acceptance criteria.
[06:48] Tomás Rueda: any blockers from our side? none immediate.
[06:51] Jesse Harper: ok awesome, we'll send notes and links after. thanks everyone.
[06:55] Leah Goldman: thanks, talk soon.
[06:58] call ends
